title: Candy Corn Bag

drivers.name: Price increase (6%)
drivers.evidence: Last week at same price (4.08) sold 3 units (x0.29 vs baseline); past promotions show noise-adjusted lift only x1.45; this is a non-promotional price hike, likely reducing demand.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 10.3. A price increase to $4.08 (6% above regular $3.85) is the only driver. Past promotions show a median lift of x2.15 vs baseline, but noise-adjusted estimate is x1.45. This is a 6% price increase, not a promotion, so it likely reduces demand. The prior week (2026-10-05) at $4.08 sold only 3 units (x0.29 vs baseline), indicating price sensitivity. The classical model suggests no lift, but that ignores price effects. We apply a downside adjustment: price increase likely suppresses demand. Evidence is strong from recent week and history of price sensitivity. Adjust multiplier down to 0.65. Spreads remain at 1.0 as no new uncertainty is introduced.

  shelf price: 4.08 (+6.0% vs regular price 3.85)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 10.3 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 23.5 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 18.6

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-85% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
